newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: War crimes tribunal prosecutor to visit Balkans.
newsitem.headline: War crimes tribunal prosecutor to visit Balkans.

text.p: The chief prosecutor of the Hague tribunal investigating war crimes in former Yugoslavia will visit the region this week for talks on cooperation with the court, the tribunal said on Wednesday.
Louise Arbour will hold ministerial-level meetings in Croatia, Bosnia and Serbia during a trip beginning on Thursday, the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia (ICTY) said.

"The purpose of this visit is to allow Justice Arbour to meet key ministers and other senior officials and to hold face-to-face discussions on the legal and practical aspects of the necessary cooperation between the office of the prosecutor and the relevant authorities," its statement said.

The tribunal, set up by the United Nations in 1993, has indicted more than 70 Serbs, Croats and Moslems for atrocities committed during the Bosnian conflict, but has been hampered by its inability to enforce the arrest of suspects still at large.

Arbour, a Canadian judge, said when she was appointed last year that her top priority would be to push for the detention of indicted suspects. "There is no single issue more important to the survival of this tribunal," she said.
